newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere to open shares to foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Solidere to open shares to foreigners.

text.p: Lebanon's biggest company Solidere said on Thursday it planned to lift all ownership restrictions on its shares and allow foreign investors and local institutions to buy them.
The changes were likely to take place in October when the distribution of shares to property owners in central Beirut was expected to be complete, Chairman Nasser Chammaa told Reuters.

"The board felt it will serve the best interests of shareholders to open up investment in the shares of the company to institutional investors all over the world and to Lebanese banks and Lebanese companies which have been excluded," Chammaa said in an interview.
Shares in Solidere, which is rebuilding war-ravaged central Beirut, cannot currently be bought by non-Arabs. Lebanese banks and most local companies are also barred from ownership.
Chammaa said the board of directors had decided to call an extraordinary shareholders' meeting to approve lifting the restrictions. The decision would also require government approval, he said.

The date of the shareholders' meeting would be announced next week. After the changes "there will be no restrictions on transferability except for the 10 percent limit on ownership of the company's shares by a single owner," Chammaa added.
